newsitem.title: FRANCE: Key Chirac fundraiser arrested in French probe.
newsitem.headline: Key Chirac fundraiser arrested in French probe.

text.p: An investigating magistrate struck at the heart of an alleged covert funding system of President Jacques Chirac's Gaullist RPR party on Thursday by ordering the arrest of the movement's former personnel chief.

Louise-Yvonne Casetta, nicknamed "la cassette" (the safe) in the party because she was regarded as its shadow treasurer, was detained by police before dawn for questioning by magistrate Patrick Desmure on suspected graft, justice sources said.

They said she was expected to be placed under judicial investigation on suspicion of misuse of corporate funds in connection with alleged illicit funding of the RPR by the construction firm Maillard et Duclos in 1992-93.
Casetta was head of personnel at party headquarters until last September but is widely regarded as having been its main secret fundraiser.
Police picked her up at her Paris home shortly after six a.m. (0500 GMT) in a technique usually reserved for suspects who they fear might try to flee.
A Paris-region company executive has testified that Casetta effectively controlled access to City of Paris public housing contracts in exchange for cash payments for Chirac's party.

Jean-Claude Pittau, former head of the Mazzotti public works contractor, told the magistrate last June that his company had paid her at least 500,000 francs ($100,000) in cash over two years, the newspaper Le Monde reported.
The paper said a company executive delivered envelopes stuffed with banknotes to Casetta in person at RPR headquarters.
Le Monde said the magistrate had already placed five businessmen under investigation for suspected corruption over their involvement in the false invoicing system.
Justice sources said Casetta worked closely with Jean-Claude Mery, a Paris consultant who is under investigation for alleged large-scale illicit fundraising on behalf of the Gaullist party.

Paris police have also held a preliminary investigation into allegations that Casetta received a fictitious 25,000 franc ($5,000) monthly salary from a subsidiary of public works giant Compagnie Generale des Eaux in 1991-94.
The Paris public prosecutor's office has recommended that she be charged in the case but charges have not yet been laid.
Her lawyer was not available for comment on the cases.
France has been plagued since 1990 with a seemingly endless series of corruption scandals involving covert funding of all the major parties through rake-offs on public contracts.
The scandals first hit the late president Francois Mitterrand's Socialist party and played a major role in its landslide general election defeat in 1993.

Graft-busting magistrates have since uncovered what they suspect was a huge covert funding system for the Gaullists based on rake-offs from public works contracts in the Paris region while Chirac was mayor of the capital.
These cases are potentially even more damaging to Chirac than the Socialist scandals were to Mitterrand, since he was personally at the head of the Paris city administration for 17 years.

In a related probe, a magistrate has opened an investigation into the wife of Chirac's successor as mayor, Jean Tiberi, who is suspected of having been paid 200,000 francs ($40,000) for a 36-page report largely copied out of a book.
